A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coastal resource use conflicts are often not only about the resource itself but about the power to define the resource, and the knowledge and values used in defining the resource.
coastal conflict resolution needs to be based on the integration of power relations, joint learning and knowledge use.
the most successful conflicts were those in which the actors were able to develop a common understanding of the problem and the solution and to develop a common identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resolution of conflicts is a long-term process and that the resolution process needs to be embedded in the overall coastal management strategy.
coastal management needs to be more conflict sensitive and conflict oriented in order to be able to deal with the complexity of resource use conflicts in coastal areas.
the integration of knowledge and power relations into coastal management is essential for sustainable resource use.
